findings.evidence: Current-gen models commonly ship windows ranging from roughly 8K tokens in older or small-tier deployments up to a million-plus tokens at the frontier, varying by model and vendor — for example, the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next card states a native 262K-token window with YaRN extension to 1M, and the GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4 cards state 1M ([1P][FACT] model cards: HF Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next; HF zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash; DeepSeek-V4 technical report, arXiv 2606.19348, and model card HF deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro — all accessed 2026-08-30, the book’s evidence cutoff; Appendix A §10); the low end of that range is the older/edge tier rather than a published figure for a current frontier model — this book’s reading of the vendor line-ups above, not a vendor statement [1P][HYPOTHESIS].
findings.issue: The sentence begins by saying current-gen models commonly ship windows “ranging from roughly 8K tokens in older or small-tier deployments up to a million-plus tokens at the frontier,” then admits the low end is “the older/edge tier rather than a published figure for a current frontier model.” That is a scope drift: the opening claim is about current-gen models, while the cited support covers only the high end. A reader can reasonably infer that current frontier models still commonly ship 8K windows, which the sentence itself later disclaims.
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite the opening clause to separate the historical/edge tier from the current frontier tier: e.g. “Older or small-tier deployments may still ship roughly 8K-token windows, while current frontier cards commonly advertise hundreds of thousands to a million-plus tokens.” Keep the cited Qwen/GLM/DeepSeek examples attached only to the frontier claim.

findings.evidence: Ch. 1, §1.1.5 (p.8): "the standing FP8-KV qualifiers are stated once in Ch. 7 §4 (the accounting-basis note)". Ch. 6, §6.6 (p.126) repeats: "(The vLLM FP8-KV blog's '54%' [S6] is a decode inter-token-latency (ITL) slope, not a memory ratio or footprint coefficient — on this book's own reading of that post's Table 3, not a vendor-stated interpretation [1P][HYPOTHESIS]; re-verify it against the post, as Ch 1 does at its KV-cache section.)"
findings.issue: Ch. 1 states the FP8-KV qualifiers are 'stated once in Ch. 7 §4,' but Ch. 6 §6.6 repeats them verbatim (the '54%' ITL-slope reading and the re-verify caveat). Either the 'stated once' claim is wrong (they appear in Ch. 1, Ch. 6, and Ch. 7), or Ch. 6's repetition was intended as a cross-reference back to Ch. 1 rather than a restatement. As written, the reader is told the qualifiers live in exactly one place, then encounters them in three.
findings.fix_instruction: Either (a) change Ch. 1's text from 'stated once in Ch. 7 §4' to 'consolidated in Ch. 7 §4, with reminders in Ch. 1 §5 and Ch. 6 §6.6', or (b) replace Ch. 6 §6.6's restatement with a cross-reference: 'see the FP8-KV accounting-basis note in Ch. 7 §4 for the standing qualifiers.'

findings.evidence: Table 1-1, input/output ratio row (p.12): "input / output ratio | ~30× | 9,200 ÷ 300 ≈ 30.7, shown at the canonical ~30×". The derivation shows 30.7 (rounded to one decimal: 9200/300 = 30.666…), but the value column and subsequent text throughout the book use '~30×' (e.g. Ch. 4 p.62: 'Input-to-output ratio: 9,200 ÷ 300 ≈ 30×'). The value 30× implies 30.0, while the derivation shows 30.7 — a rounding of 30.67 to the nearest integer gives 31, not 30. The '~30×' is an approximation but the derivation column shows 30.7, which rounds to 31 not 30 at integer precision.
findings.issue: The table simultaneously shows '~30×' in the value column and '≈30.7' in the derivation. Rounding 30.666… to an integer gives 31, not 30. The book uses '~30×' throughout as a convenient round number, but the derivation column's '≈30.7' makes the rounding down to 30 inconsistent — a reader recomputing 9,200 ÷ 300 gets 30.67, which does not round to 30 at integer precision. The '~' does heavy lifting here but the derivation column undermines it.
findings.fix_instruction: Either change the derivation cell to '~30× (9,200 ÷ 300 ≈ 30.7, rounded down for convenience)' making the deliberate down-rounding explicit, or change the value to '~31×' for integer consistency. The current juxtaposition of '~30×' with '≈30.7' invites a reader to check and find a mismatch.
